metaDescription: Six countertop ice makers compared by ice type, real output, tank size and cleaning, from bullet cubes to soft nugget, so you can pick the right machine.
expertTake: The EUHOMY 44 lb Nugget is the pick for most households that want chewable ice without a premium price, and the GoveeLife 60 lb is the choice if you host often and want the most output. The Silonn is the value pick for portable bullet ice. Skip a countertop machine if you only need a few trays a week, because a freezer does that job with no upkeep.
introParagraphs: A countertop ice maker promises endless ice in minutes, but the headline number on the box rarely matches what a kitchen sees. The pounds per day figure is a best case, the ice type changes how you use it, and the maintenance burden is higher than most buyers expect.

This guide explains how bullet and nugget machines make ice, why scale and warm rooms cut output, and how tank size drives how often you refill. The picks above give the short list, and the detailed reviews below show which machine fits which household.

buyingCriteria.explanation: Bullet machines freeze ice onto a metal probe and release hard, clear cubes, while nugget machines scrape a frozen layer into soft, chewable pellets. Nugget costs more and is slower to start but is the preferred ice for chewing and for cocktails. The bullet machines here, the Silonn, Frigidaire and Antarctic Star, are rated at 26 pounds a day. The EUHOMY nugget models reach 34 and 44 pounds, and the GoveeLife claims 60.

Rated pounds per 24 hours is measured under ideal conditions, and a warm room or warm tap water can cut real output by roughly a fifth. A good rule is to plan for about 80 percent of the rating and ignore 24 hour figures unless you will run the machine around the clock. Use rated output to compare machines, not to promise yourself exact quantities. A household that wants 20 pounds in a day should look at the 34 pound EUHOMY or higher.

A small tank means constant refilling, and refilling is the most common complaint about countertop machines. The Silonn holds 1.2 liters and the Frigidaire 2.1 quarts, while the EUHOMY 44 carries 1.8 liters and the GoveeLife combines 2.2 and 4.9 liters. The Govee yields over 15 pounds of ice per fill, which is the best in this guide. If you entertain, tank size matters more than first batch speed.

Mineral scale builds on the evaporator or probe and is the main reason these machines die early. Look for a real self-clean cycle, an easy drain, and water you can run through it. The Govee offers a 30 minute descale mode, the EUHOMY 44 a 20 minute cycle, and the Silonn a 30 minute clean. Hard water means you should use filtered water or plan to descale monthly.

Most of these machines make ice but do not keep it frozen, so cubes melt in the basket and the meltwater is recycled. The Frigidaire listing says this explicitly. If you want ice for tomorrow, you must scoop into a freezer. Basket sizes also differ, from 1.3 pounds on the Silonn to 3.5 pounds on the Govee.

Nugget machines are taller, and the EUHOMY 44 needs about 14.95 inches of height, so measure under your cabinets. Compressors make a rattling and gurgling noise during harvest, and the numbers given by makers are best case. Give any ice maker an inch or two of clearance for ventilation. A smart machine like the GoveeLife adds app control but no extra ice.

specDecoder.meaning: This is the amount of ice the machine could make in a day of continuous running under favorable conditions. It is a capacity figure, not a daily supply, because the machine stops when the basket fills.
specDecoder.watchFor: Ratings assume a cool room and cold water. The 60 lb Govee and 44 lb EUHOMY lose output in a warm kitchen.

specDecoder.meaning: This is the time from a cold start to the first set of cubes. It describes responsiveness, not hourly throughput, because later cycles can take longer as the basket fills.
specDecoder.watchFor: The 6 minute claims on the Silonn and Antarctic Star are first-batch times and do not mean 26 pounds an hour.

specDecoder.meaning: This is how much water the reservoir holds before you must refill. Divide it by the machine's water use per pound to estimate ice per fill.
specDecoder.watchFor: A big combined tank, like the Govee's, is worth more than a quick first batch if you throw parties.

specDecoder.meaning: Noise is the sound level during operation, and ice makers have a louder harvest or drop moment than the compressor hum.
specDecoder.watchFor: Listed figures such as the Govee's 40 dB are best-case modes. Real noise also depends on the counter and the room.

howWeEvaluated.title: Ice type and output
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared bullet and nugget machines by how they make ice and by the rated pounds per 24 hours, using the real range from the 26 pound Silonn to the 60 pound GoveeLife.

howWeEvaluated.title: Tank and basket size
howWeEvaluated.description: We looked at the water tank and ice basket on each machine because they decide how often you must refill or empty. The Govee's combined tanks sit at one end and the Silonn's 1.2 liter tank at the other.

howWeEvaluated.title: Cleaning and scale control
howWeEvaluated.description: We weighed the quality of each self-clean cycle and how easy it is to drain, since scale shortens life. The Govee's 30 minute descale and the Frigidaire's drain plug scored well.

howWeEvaluated.title: Fit and noise
howWeEvaluated.description: We checked footprints and heights to see what fits under cabinets, and weighed claimed noise levels against typical compressor behavior. The EUHOMY 44 is the tallest, while the Silonn is the lightest at 13.7 pounds.

cards.label: Bullet ice
cards.text: Hard, clear cubes made in batches by a probe. Better for slow-melting drinks and cheaper to buy. The Silonn, Frigidaire and Antarctic Star all fall here at 26 pounds a day.

cards.label: Nugget ice
cards.text: Soft, porous pellets made continuously by an auger. Better for chewing and cocktails, but more complex to maintain. The EUHOMY 34, EUHOMY 44 and GoveeLife make nugget ice.

howToChoose.note: Choose bullet for occasional drinks and portability. Choose nugget if you chew ice or use a lot of it.

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: High daily output, a big basket and tanks that need few refills. Remember that rated output assumes cool conditions, so size up.

cards.label: In this comparison
cards.text: The GoveeLife 60 lb is the best fit, with a 3.5 pound basket and tanks that make more than 15 pounds per fill. The EUHOMY 44 lb is the next choice if you want nugget without smart features.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: You chew ice or serve a crowd, which points to the EUHOMY 44 lb or GoveeLife 60 lb. You also hate refilling, where bigger tanks matter.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: You make iced coffee occasionally, where the Silonn or Antarctic Star is enough. You have limited counter space and the 34 lb EUHOMY covers nugget needs.

maintenance.interval: Weekly or every two weeks of use
maintenance.why: Biofilm and mineral deposits form in the reservoir and on the evaporator. A cycle keeps ice tasting clean and the machine producing at rated speed.

maintenance.task: Descale with citric or approved cleaner
maintenance.why: Limescale on the evaporator insulates it and slows ice making. Run the cleaner through, then rinse thoroughly.
Standing water breeds slime. Drain and dry before moving the machine or putting it away.
Ice touches these directly, and residue picks up flavors. Wash with mild soap and rinse.
Compressors need airflow to shed heat. Blocked vents cut output and shorten compressor life.

faq.q: Is nugget ice worth it over bullet ice?
faq.a: If you chew ice or want it in cocktails and soda, yes. Nugget is soft and absorbs flavor, but the machines cost more and need more upkeep. Bullet ice is harder, clearer and fine for most drinks.

faq.q: How much should I plan to spend?
faq.a: Bullet machines like the Silonn and Antarctic Star are the least expensive tier. Nugget machines cost more, and a smart machine like the GoveeLife sits at the top. Budget for filtered water and cleaner as ongoing costs.

faq.q: How long do countertop ice makers last?
faq.a: Lifespans depend heavily on cleaning, because scale is the main killer. Regular self-clean cycles and descaling extend life. Machines left with standing water often fail early.

faq.q: Does 26 lb per day mean I get 26 lb of ice?
faq.a: Not usually. That figure is the machine's best-case rate in cool conditions. A warm kitchen or a full basket lowers it, so plan for around 80 percent.

faq.q: Will a countertop ice maker keep my ice frozen?
faq.a: No, most of these do not. They make ice and recycle melt water, so cubes shrink in the basket. Move ice to a freezer if you want to keep it.
You can, but hard water causes scale and cloudy ice. Filtered or softened water reduces scale and helps the machine last. If your water is hard, descale more often.

products.name: EUHOMY 44 lb Nugget Ice Maker Countertop
products.description:
Nugget ice is made differently from the hard bullet cubes in cheaper machines. Water freezes onto a cold evaporator wall, and an auger scrapes it off and compresses the flakes into soft, chewable pellets. This model is rated at up to 44 pounds per 24 hours, the highest figure among the machines here that make true nugget ice at a home-appliance size.

The larger 1.8 liter tank is the practical reason to choose it over the 34 pound sibling in this lineup, which carries 1.1 liters. The machine takes about 13.9 by 9.85 by 14.95 inches of counter, so it is taller than the bullet machines, and you should check cabinet clearance before buying. Against the GoveeLife it gives up the smart features and the very high rating, but it is simpler and has fewer parts to fail.

Nugget machines demand more upkeep than bullet machines because the evaporator and auger live in constant contact with water. Run the 20 minute self-clean cycle on schedule, descale with citric or manufacturer-approved cleaner when you see white crust, and use filtered water where the supply is hard. The rated output is a best case in cool kitchens, and you should expect noticeably less in a warm room.
products.bestFor: Households that want soft, chewable nugget ice in volume without stepping up to a smart, high-end machine.
pros: Highest nugget output of the simple machines in this guide
Larger 1.8 L tank than the 34 lb sibling means fewer refills
One-touch self-clean cycle takes about twenty minutes
Soft nugget ice absorbs drink flavor and is easy to chew
cons: Taller body needs cabinet clearance above the counter
Auger and evaporator need regular descaling in hard water
Output drops in a warm kitchen compared with the rating

products.name: GoveeLife Smart Nugget Ice Maker Pro, 60 lb
products.description:
This is the heavy hitter of the roundup. A rating of 60 pounds per 24 hours is well above the 44 pounds of the EUHOMY and about double what the bullet machines claim, and the dual tank system pairs a small 2.2 liter tank with a 4.9 liter one so the machine can make more than 15 pounds of ice from a single fill. That matters for parties and for households that go through a lot of ice, because refilling is the chore that makes countertop machines annoying.

It adds app and voice control, scheduling and cleaning reminders, which are conveniences rather than ice-making features, and some owners will see that as extra failure points. The 3.5 pound basket is more than twice the 1.5 pound basket on the Frigidaire, so you get a deeper reserve between cycles. The listed 40 decibel noise figure is a best case that depends on the mode and the room, so treat it as a promise of a quieter machine than average rather than silence.

The deeper ownership issue is scale. Two cleaning modes, a quick 10 minute refresh and a 30 minute descale, exist because limescale is the number one thing that kills these machines. Use them on schedule, keep the water softer than raw hard tap if you can, and expect that a machine making this much ice will also lose output faster if you neglect the evaporator.
products.bestFor: Heavy ice users and party hosts who want the largest output and fewest refills from one countertop machine.
pros: Highest rated output in the lineup at 60 lb per day
Dual tank system gives more than 15 lb per single fill
Deep 3.5 lb basket holds far more than the smaller machines do
Two cleaning modes include a 30 minute descale cycle
cons: Largest and most complex machine with more things to fail
Smart features add convenience but nothing to the ice itself
Rated output is a best case that shrinks in warm rooms

products.name: EUHOMY 34 lb Nugget Ice Maker Countertop
products.description:
If the 44 pound machine is more nugget ice than you need, this is the sensible step down. It makes the same soft, chewable nugget ice through the same auger-and-evaporator process, but at a rated 34 pounds a day and a smaller body of about 11 by 9 by 12.6 inches. A household of two or three that wants chewable ice for drinks will rarely run into the output ceiling.

The smaller 1.1 liter tank is the main compromise. It will empty quickly if the machine runs most of the day, and the Add Water and Ice Full alerts will become part of your routine. Against the EUHOMY 44 at 1.8 liters it needs more refills, and against the GoveeLife with a combined tank over 7 liters it needs many more. In return it takes less counter space and is easier to tuck into a kitchen corner.

Cleaning follows the same self-clean routine as the larger model, started by holding a button for about 5 seconds. Do it on schedule, because a nugget machine with scale on the evaporator makes weaker and slower ice.
products.bestFor: Small households that want nugget ice on a counter without paying for or housing a bigger machine.
pros: Nugget ice from a smaller machine that fits tighter spaces
Rated 34 lb per day is plenty for two or three people
Clear window and alerts show ice level and water status
Self-clean starts with a single five second button hold
cons: Small 1.1 L tank needs frequent refilling at high use
Smaller output than the 44 lb model if you host often

products.name: Antarctic Star 26 lb Bullet Ice Maker, 6 Minute Cycle
products.description:
A bullet ice machine makes cubes by dipping a metal probe into water and freezing a layer of ice onto each finger, which then drops into a basket. It is a batch process, so the machine makes eight or nine cubes, pauses to harvest them, and starts again. This Antarctic Star claims a 6 minute first batch and a rating of 26 pounds per day, the same output class as the Frigidaire and Silonn here.

The selling points are the two cube sizes, a carry handle and a footprint of roughly 8.7 by 11.5 by 11.6 inches that fits RV counters, dorm rooms and a small kitchen. Against the Silonn it offers a similar profile, and the practical difference is the shorter claimed first batch rather than the ice itself. The company also claims lower energy use and low noise, but treat those as marketing numbers that were not independently verified. Compared with the EUHOMY nugget machines it makes harder, clearer cubes that melt more slowly in a glass but cannot be chewed comfortably.

Maintenance is the same as other bullet machines: use the self-clean cycle weekly, or after two weeks of idleness, and drain the water tank when you finish. Bullet machines do not store ice, so the cubes begin melting in the basket and the machine recycles that water to make more.
products.bestFor: Occasional entertainers, RV travelers and dorm users who want cheap, fast bullet ice from a small machine.
pros: Six minute first batch makes drinks quickly after startup
Two cube sizes suit both small drinks and larger glasses
Small footprint and handle make it easy to move around
Self-cleaning cycle covers the weekly maintenance routine
cons: Bullet ice cannot be chewed comfortably like nugget
Ice melts in the basket because it is not an ice storage unit
Energy and noise claims are marketing figures, not measurements

products.name: Silonn 26 lb Portable Bullet Ice Maker with Handle
products.description:
The Silonn is built around the idea that a countertop ice maker should be easy to carry. At 13.7 pounds with a sturdy handle and a body of about 8.7 by 11.4 by 11.6 inches, it moves from kitchen to patio to camper without effort. The compressor can make nine bullet cubes in about 6 minutes and the listing rates it at 26 pounds a day, which is enough for most small gatherings.

The basket stores only about 1.3 pounds, and the 1.2 liter water tank is modest. You will check it often if you are serving a crowd, and the indicator lights tell you when to add water or when the basket is full. Compared with the Frigidaire, which has a 1.5 pound basket and a 2.1 quart tank, the Silonn is almost identical in capacity, and it is the lighter machine. Compared with the EUHOMY nugget models it makes a harder cube that is better for a long-lasting glass and a poor choice for chewing.

To clean it, remove the basket, add water, and hold the CLEAN button for 5 seconds, then wait about 30 minutes. Do that regularly, because the machine recirculates melt water and mineral deposits show up first as cloudy cubes.
products.bestFor: Campers, tailgaters and anyone who moves a small ice maker between rooms or vehicles.
pros: Light 13.7 lb body with a sturdy handle is easy to carry
Makes nine cubes in about six minutes after startup
Indicator lights show when to add water or empty ice
Self-clean cycle is simple and takes about thirty minutes
cons: Small basket holds about a pound and a third of ice
Bullet cubes are too hard and cold to chew comfortably
Output is no higher than the Frigidaire or Antarctic Star

products.name: Frigidaire 26 lb Countertop Bullet Ice Maker, Black Stainless
products.description:
The Frigidaire is the pick for people who want a familiar appliance name and a finish that looks at home beside other kitchen appliances. Like the Silonn and Antarctic Star it uses a probe-and-harvest bullet process, making nine cubes about every 7 minutes at a rating of 26 pounds per day. The black stainless body, LED control panel and clear viewing window make it easy to monitor ice level and cycles.

Its 2.1 quart water tank is a practical edge, since it is a bit larger than the Silonn's, and the 1.5 pound basket is also a little larger. A drain plug makes emptying and cleaning straightforward, which is the hidden detail that decides whether you will actually clean it. It is slightly slower than the 6 minute machines, but output over a day is the same rating, so most buyers will not notice. Compared with the nugget machines here, it cannot make chewable ice.

The important caveat in the listing is that this machine makes ice but does not keep it frozen. Ice melts in the basket and the water is recycled, so if you want a stock for later, move it to the freezer.
products.bestFor: Buyers who want a recognizable brand and an easy-to-drain bullet ice maker for everyday kitchen use.
pros: Easy-drain plug simplifies emptying and cleaning the reservoir
Larger 2.1 qt tank than the Silonn reduces refills
LED panel and clear window show cycle and ice level
Familiar brand and finish suit a kitchen counter setup well
cons: Slower 7 minute cycle than the 6 minute competitors
Does not keep ice frozen, so cubes melt in the basket
